name: rtk-dangerous-actions-blocker
description: Deprecated: use block-destructive-commands, which shares this policy's destructive-command table. rtk#1007. Same table as block-destructive-commands: blocks root/home/.git deletes, force/delete/mirror pushes, reset --hard, clean -f, switch --discard, IaC destroy, cloud deletes, DB drops, lockouts; asks rm -rf off rtk's safe list, one named kubectl delete, bare lease, stash drop, prunes; dry-run flags pass. Own rows block credential-file reads (.env, keys, ~/.ssh) and echo or inline *_API_KEY/_SECRET/_TOKEN. Skips file rows in container exec. [Best-effort in Devin by a PreToolUse hook shipped with the plugin's hooks.json (witnessed blocking on Devin CLI 3000.11.3 (local session), Windows, 2026-10-08). In the vendor's own words, plugin hooks are 'currently best effort and fail open -- if a hook fails to load or run, the session continues without it -- so don't rely on them for crucial guardrails yet', documented for local Devin sessions (the CLI and Devin Desktop) only. The hook command expands $DEVIN_PLUGIN_ROOT, an environment variable the vendor documents hook commands receive; whether that expansion happens inside a hooks.json command string is documented, not witnessed here. The hook needs git and a Python 3.11+ on PATH. Repo-wide git-hook and CI coverage still needs `chock sync`.]
